components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
彐 here depicts a broom, standing in for 帚 in the traditional form 歸 — the image of a wife returning home with her broom gave 归 its meaning 'to return.'

example.hanzi: 每年秋天，大雁都会回归南方过冬。
example.pinyin: Měi nián qiūtiān, dàyàn dōu huì huíguī nánfāng guòdōng.
example.english: Every autumn, the wild geese return south for the winter.
example.fact: Atlantic salmon can swim thousands of kilometers back to the exact river where they hatched, guided partly by sensing Earth's magnetic field and partly by the unique chemical scent of their home stream. This precise homing ability, called natal river fidelity, remains one of the most striking examples of long-distance animal navigation.

meanings: abbr. for 公共汽車|公共汽车[gong1 gong4 qi4 che1]
car belonging to an organization and used by its members
abbr. for 公務用車|公务用车[gong1 wu4 yong4 che1]

components.note: 八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'

example.hanzi: 他每天坐公车去上班。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān zuò gōngchē qù shàngbān.
example.english: He takes the bus to work every day.
example.fact: The world's first public bus-like service, the “carrosses à cinq sols,” began running fixed routes through Paris in 1662 at the urging of mathematician Blaise Pascal, charging a flat fare of five sols per ride. The venture folded within a few years, and organized urban mass transit did not reappear in a lasting form until the 19th century.

components.note: 宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
入 (enter, put away) — 全 pictures something being placed into safekeeping.
玉 (jade) — a valuable treasure kept whole and undamaged, giving 全 its meaning of 'complete' or 'entire.'
巾 (cloth) — the bottom half of a belt, hanging straight down.
Above the cloth, the strokes crease as if folded at the waist — depicting a belt or sash, the source of 带's meaning 'belt, band,' later 'to bring, carry along.'

example.hanzi: 上车以后，请先系好安全带。
example.pinyin: Shàng chē yǐhòu, qǐng xiān jìhǎo ānquándài.
example.english: After getting in the car, please buckle your seat belt first.
example.fact: Swedish engineer Nils Bohlin invented the modern three-point seat belt in 1959 while working at Volvo, replacing the far less effective two-point lap belt. Volvo made the patent freely available to every other car manufacturer, a decision credited with saving hundreds of thousands of lives worldwide in the decades since.

components.note: 州 depicts small dots of land, like islands, surrounded by the curving lines of a river (川) — the origin of its meaning 'state, region.'
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.

example.hanzi: 加州州长将在明天发表演讲。
example.pinyin: Jiāzhōu zhōuzhǎng jiāng zài míngtiān fābiǎo yǎnjiǎng.
example.english: The governor of California will give a speech tomorrow.
example.fact: In 2003, California governor Gray Davis became only the second U.S. state governor in history to be removed through a recall election, made possible because California's constitution lets voters petition for a special election at any point in a governor's term. Arnold Schwarzenegger won the simultaneous replacement vote and was sworn in weeks later.

components.note: 丹 depicts a pellet of red cinnabar mineral, dug from a mine — the source of its meaning 'cinnabar, red, pellet.'
尸 here represents a reclining or seated human figure; paired with 匕 (another simplified person shape), 尼 originally pictured two people close together, an old source of the meaning 'near.'

匕 is a simplified rendering of a person shape; combined with 尸 it reinforces the original image of two figures side by side. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound to write Buddhist and foreign terms such as 尼姑 (Buddhist nun) and 尼泊尔 (Nepal).
斤 depicts an axe; 斯's early meaning was 'to split, to tear apart,' pictured by the axe cutting something in two.

其 (qí) is the phonetic element; its ancient reading was closer to today's sī. The character is now mainly used as a transliteration syllable in foreign names and loanwords, as in 丹尼斯 (Dennis) and 巴士 (bus).

example.hanzi: 丹尼斯是我们公司新来的工程师。
example.pinyin: Dānísī shì wǒmen gōngsī xīn lái de gōngchéngshī.
example.english: Dennis is the new engineer at our company.
example.fact: Dennis Ritchie, a computer scientist at Bell Labs, co-created the Unix operating system in 1969 and then designed the C programming language in the early 1970s to help rewrite it. C went on to directly influence nearly every major programming language that followed, from C++ and Java to Python, making it one of the most consequential pieces of software ever written.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — held in a hand, the image behind 布's meaning 'cloth' and, by extension, 'to spread out, distribute.'
罒 (a net) — 置 originally meant to set a net in place
直 (zhí) gives a sound close to 置's reading zhì, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 我们花了一个下午布置婚礼现场。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen huāle yí gè xiàwǔ bùzhì hūnlǐ xiànchǎng.
example.english: We spent an entire afternoon setting up the wedding venue.
example.fact: NASA's Mission Control Center in Houston was deliberately arranged in tiers, with flight controllers seated by function so information could flow upward from technical specialists to the flight director without anyone needing to shout across the room. That tiered layout, first used for the Gemini and Apollo missions, is still the basic model for mission control rooms today.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

升 is a pictograph of an ancient grain-measuring ladle or vessel. Scooping and lifting grain with it gave rise to the extended meaning 'to rise, to ascend,' and the character also survives today as a unit of volume equal to one liter.

example.hanzi: 气温一直在上升，今天特别热。
example.pinyin: Qìwēn yìzhí zài shàngshēng, jīntiān tèbié rè.
example.english: The temperature has kept rising, and it's especially hot today.
example.fact: Mount Everest is still growing by roughly 4 millimeters a year because the Indian tectonic plate continues to push into and slide beneath the Eurasian plate, a collision that first raised the Himalayas around 50 million years ago. Precise GPS measurements placed on the summit in recent years have confirmed the peak's ongoing upward creep.

meanings: to do what one is told

components.note: 口 (mouth) — words spoken by a mouth are what reach the ear, giving 听 its meaning 'to listen.'
斤 stands in for the ear in this simplified character — the target that spoken words reach.
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

example.hanzi: 这只狗很听话，从不乱叫。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī gǒu hěn tīnghuà, cóng bù luàn jiào.
example.english: This dog is very obedient and never barks without reason.
example.fact: Border collies are widely considered the most trainable dog breed, and one named Chaser learned to recognize the names of over 1,000 individual objects in tests run by researchers at Wofford College. Her handlers found she could correctly retrieve a specific toy by name even when it was mixed in with dozens of others she had never fetched that way before.

components.note: 攵 (a hand with an implement) — relates to 收's meaning 'to receive, collect, harvest.'
丩 (jiū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shōu.
艹 (grass) — 藏 relates to hiding something among vegetation.
臧 (zāng) gives a rhyme close to cáng, sharing a similar initial.

example.hanzi: 他从小就喜欢收藏邮票。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xǐhuan shōucáng yóupiào.
example.english: He has loved collecting stamps since he was a child.
example.fact: Charles Darwin was an obsessive beetle collector as a young man, and his lifelong habit of cataloguing small variations between specimens later shaped the observational skills he brought to developing the theory of evolution by natural selection. He once reportedly popped a rare beetle into his mouth to keep his hands free for catching two more.

components.note: 尽 simplifies the traditional 盡, which pictured a hand scraping the last bits of food out of a vessel. The image of scraping something completely clean gave 尽 its meaning 'to exhaust, to the utmost, until the end.'
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 沿着这条路走到尽头就是海边。
example.pinyin: Yánzhe zhè tiáo lù zǒu dào jìntóu jiùshì hǎibiān.
example.english: Walk along this road to the end and you'll reach the seaside.
example.fact: The Trans-Siberian Railway's main line runs 9,289 kilometers from Moscow to Vladivostok, making it the longest continuous railway line in the world. Crossing it end to end takes about a week of near-constant travel through eight time zones.

components.note: 氵 (water) — leaking is described using the water radical, whether literal or figurative.
世 (shì) gives a sound distantly related to xiè, having drifted apart over time.
雨 (rain) — 露 names a form of moisture related to weather.
路 (lù) gives the sound — an exact match with 露.

example.hanzi: 公司担心客户的信息会被泄露。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī dānxīn kèhù de xìnxī huì bèi xièlòu.
example.english: The company is worried that customer information might be leaked.
example.fact: In 2016, an anonymous source leaked 11.5 million confidential documents from the Panamanian law firm Mossack Fonseca, an event now known as the Panama Papers. The files exposed how numerous world leaders and wealthy individuals used offshore shell companies to hide assets, triggering resignations and investigations in dozens of countries.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 治 relates to managing or controlling the flow of water, such as flood control.
台 (a platform, structure) — a structure used to direct and control water gave 治 its meaning 'to govern' or 'to manage.'
心 (heart/mind) — 愈 relates to the mind or body recovering.
俞 (yú) gives a sound close to yù, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 医生说这种病是可以治愈的。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō zhè zhǒng bìng shì kěyǐ zhìyù de.
example.english: The doctor said this illness can be cured.
example.fact: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 almost by accident, after noticing that mold had killed off bacteria in a petri dish he had carelessly left uncovered. It took over a decade before Howard Florey and Ernst Chain developed methods to mass-produce the drug, and penicillin went on to save an estimated hundreds of millions of lives from bacterial infections that were previously untreatable.

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'
A pictograph of half of a split tree trunk, shown in cross-section (compare 爿, the other half) — the source of 片's meaning 'a thin slice, piece.'

example.hanzi: 他递给我一张名片，上面印着他的职位。
example.pinyin: Tā dì gěi wǒ yì zhāng míngpiàn, shàngmiàn yìnzhe tā de zhíwèi.
example.english: He handed me a business card with his title printed on it.
example.fact: In Japan, the exchange of business cards, known as meishi, follows a strict etiquette in which the card is presented and received with both hands, held so the recipient can read it right away, and never written on or pocketed in front of the giver. Breaking these unwritten rules is considered a minor social misstep in Japanese business culture.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 勒 relates to tightening or restraining with force.
革 (gé) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading lēi has diverged considerably.
糸 (thread) — thick strands twisted into a rope
冖 (a covering) — the ceiling or beam the rope hangs from

example.hanzi: 有人试图用照片勒索这位明星。
example.pinyin: Yǒurén shìtú yòng zhàopiàn lèsuǒ zhè wèi míngxīng.
example.english: Someone tried to blackmail the star using photographs.
example.fact: The 2017 WannaCry ransomware attack encrypted files on more than 200,000 computers across 150 countries in a single weekend, demanding Bitcoin payments to unlock them. It exploited a Windows vulnerability that had been stockpiled by the U.S. National Security Agency and leaked online just a month earlier, and it briefly crippled parts of the United Kingdom's National Health Service.

components.note: 大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.

example.hanzi: 晚上天上挂满了星星。
example.pinyin: Wǎnshang tiānshàng guàmǎnle xīngxing.
example.english: The sky was full of stars at night.
example.fact: The aurora borealis, or northern lights, forms when charged particles from the solar wind collide with oxygen and nitrogen molecules high in Earth's atmosphere, exciting them enough to emit light. Oxygen collisions typically produce green or red light, while nitrogen tends to glow blue or purple, and the display is only visible because Earth's magnetic field funnels the particles toward the poles.

components.note: 阝 (mound, place) marks a location.
百 (hundred, many) sits beside it — a large, unfamiliar place, giving 陌 its meaning as a raised path between fields, and later, its role in 陌生 ('unfamiliar').
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.

example.hanzi: 在这座城市，我感到很陌生。
example.pinyin: Zài zhè zuò chéngshì, wǒ gǎndào hěn mòshēng.
example.english: I feel like a stranger in this city.
example.fact: Many migratory birds, including the European robin, can sense Earth's magnetic field through a light-sensitive protein in their eyes, allowing them to navigate across completely unfamiliar terrain during their seasonal journeys. Experiments have shown this magnetic sense can be disrupted by certain wavelengths of light and even by weak radio-frequency noise.

components.note: 冏 (bright, a window admitting light) — appears in 商's ancient form, though its exact link to 'commerce, to discuss' is unclear today.
章 — a graphic element whose original contribution to the character's meaning has been lost over time.
土 (earth) — 场 relates to a flat open area of ground, such as a field or venue.
昜 (yáng) gives a hint of the sound — 场 is pronounced chǎng, a connection that has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 周末我们经常去商场逛街。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen jīngcháng qù shāngchǎng guàngjiē.
example.english: On weekends, we often go window-shopping at the mall.
example.fact: The Southdale Center, which opened in Edina, Minnesota in 1956, is generally credited as the first fully enclosed, climate-controlled shopping mall in the world. Its Austrian-born architect, Victor Gruen, designed it to recreate the feel of a European town square indoors, though he later grew critical of how the mall format he pioneered reshaped American suburbs.

components.note: 着 keeps 目 (eye) at its base, from its ancestor 著's association with fixing one's attention on something — extended to meanings like attaching to, touching, or, as in 着迷, being visually captivated.

The remaining upper strokes are a worn-down trace of 艹 (grass), from 著's original link to plants growing and clinging to soil, later extended metaphorically to something 'sticking' or 'attaching' to a person.
辶 (to walk) — 迷 originally described losing one's way while walking, extending to 'confused, obsessed.'
米 (mǐ) gives a sound distantly related to mí, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 弟弟最近对拼图特别着迷。
example.pinyin: Dìdi zuìjìn duì pīntú tèbié zháomí.
example.english: My younger brother has been especially fascinated with puzzles lately.
example.fact: During the Dutch “tulip mania” of 1636 to 1637, buyers became so fixated on rare tulip bulbs that a single bulb of the prized Semper Augustus variety reportedly traded for more than ten times the annual income of a skilled craftsman. Prices collapsed within weeks, and the episode is still cited as one of history's earliest recorded speculative bubbles.

components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'

example.hanzi: 请尽快回复我的邮件。
example.pinyin: Qǐng jǐnkuài huífù wǒ de yóujiàn.
example.english: Please reply to my email as soon as possible.
example.fact: Because radio signals travel at the speed of light, a message sent to a rover on Mars takes anywhere from about 4 to 24 minutes to arrive depending on the planets' positions in their orbits, and a reply takes just as long to come back. Engineers at NASA account for this delay by having rovers execute pre-planned sequences of commands rather than waiting for real-time instructions.

components.note: 田 (field) — 当 originally referred to two fields of matching value, the root of its sense 'to correspond to, equivalent,' later extended to 'exactly at' a given time or place, as in 当晚 'on that very evening.'

尚 (shàng) is the historical phonetic element, its ancient reading close to dāng before the two diverged; 尚's own sense of 'still, yet' also colors 当's meaning of something holding precisely at one moment.
日 (sun) — the sun is what disappears as evening falls
免 (to escape, avoid) — pictured as the sun slipping away, giving 晚 its sense of 'late, evening'

example.hanzi: 演出结束后，当晚剧组就庆祝到很晚。
example.pinyin: Yǎnchū jiéshù hòu, dāngwǎn jùzǔ jiù qìngzhù dào hěn wǎn.
example.english: After the show ended, the cast celebrated late into that very night.
example.fact: The RMS Titanic struck an iceberg shortly before midnight on April 14, 1912, and sank in the early hours of April 15, with roughly 1,500 people dying in the frigid North Atlantic waters that same night. Investigations afterward found that the nearby ship California had spotted distress rockets but did not respond, a failure that led to major changes in maritime radio-watch rules.

components.note: The 曲-shaped top pictures a bundle of bamboo strips, an ancient book.
八 below pictures two hands supporting the book, giving 典 its meaning 'classic text, standard.'
礻 (spirit, altar) — 礼 relates to ceremony and rites performed before the spirits.
乚 reflects the character's phonetic root, though its exact link to the modern reading lǐ is unclear today.

example.hanzi: 毕业典礼将在大礼堂举行。
example.pinyin: Bìyè diǎnlǐ jiāng zài dà lǐtáng jǔxíng.
example.english: The graduation ceremony will be held in the main hall.
example.fact: The modern Olympic torch relay was introduced at the 1936 Berlin Games, devised by German organizing committee official Carl Diem to link the ancient Games at Olympia with the modern revival. The tradition has continued at nearly every Olympics since, even though the ancient Greek Olympics themselves never actually featured any torch relay at all.

components.note: 马 (horse) shows 驾 relates to driving or controlling an animal or vehicle.
加 (jiā) gives a sound close to jià, differing mainly in tone.
灬 (fire) — relates to 照's meaning 'to shine, illuminate; photograph.'
昭 (zhāo) gives a sound hint — 照 is pronounced zhào, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 他去年才拿到驾照。
example.pinyin: Tā qùnián cái nádào jiàzhào.
example.english: He only got his driver's license last year.
example.fact: New Jersey became the first U.S. state to require a license for all drivers in 1913, though early licenses were often issued with little more than a signature and a small fee, without any road test. Mandatory driving exams did not become common across the United States until the 1930s, decades after cars had already become widespread.

meanings: to take part in a competition

components.note: 彡 (shān) is the historical phonetic component of 参; sound change over time has left little resemblance to the modern reading cān
贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赛 originally related to offering valuables, later coming to mean 'to compete.'
宀 (mián) gives a sound distantly related to sài, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 今年有上百个国家参赛。
example.pinyin: Jīnnián yǒu shàng bǎi gè guójiā cānsài.
example.english: This year, over a hundred countries are competing.
example.fact: The ancient Olympic Games began at Olympia in Greece in 776 BC and continued to be held every four years for nearly 1,200 years before Roman emperor Theodosius I banned them in 393 AD as part of a suppression of pagan festivals. That makes the ancient Games one of the longest-running organized sporting traditions in recorded history.

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — 鸭 names a type of bird, the duck.
甲 (jiǎ) gives a sound distantly related to 鸭's reading yā, having drifted apart over time.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 池塘里有几只鸭子在游泳。
example.pinyin: Chítáng lǐ yǒu jǐ zhī yāzi zài yóuyǒng.
example.english: There are several ducks swimming in the pond.
example.fact: A duck's feathers stay dry in water because a gland near the base of its tail, called the uropygial gland, produces an oil that the duck spreads over its feathers while grooming. This waterproof coating, combined with tightly interlocking feather barbs, traps a layer of air next to the skin that also helps keep the bird insulated in cold water.

components.note: 业 simplifies 業, a pictograph of a notched wooden rack used to hang bells and chime-stones or to post public notices. The association with a fixed workstation or assigned task gave rise to 业's meanings 'occupation, trade, undertaking.'

余 was originally a pictograph of a simple pole-and-thatch shelter. It was later borrowed for its sound to write 餘 ('surplus, remaining'); the modern simplification dropped the food radical 食 and left 余 to stand for that meaning directly, as in 业余, 'outside one's main occupation.'

example.hanzi: 摄影只是他的业余爱好。
example.pinyin: Shèyǐng zhǐshì tā de yèyú àihào.
example.english: Photography is just his amateur hobby.
example.fact: Comet Hale-Bopp, one of the brightest comets of the 20th century, was discovered independently in 1995 by two amateur astronomers, Alan Hale and Thomas Bopp, both observing on their own time with backyard telescopes rather than as part of any professional survey. It remained visible to the naked eye for a record 18 months.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 炸 relates to a sudden burst of fire, an explosion.
乍 depicts something happening abruptly — combined with fire, giving 炸 its meaning 'to explode, to deep-fry.'
艹 (grass/plant) — many traditional medicines were made from plants and herbs
约 (yuē) gives a sound related to 药's reading yào, from an older, closer pronunciation link

example.hanzi: 工人用炸药炸开了这块岩石。
example.pinyin: Gōngrén yòng zhàyào zhàkāile zhè kuài yánshí.
example.english: The workers used explosives to blast open this rock.
example.fact: Swedish chemist Alfred Nobel invented dynamite in 1867 by stabilizing the notoriously unpredictable explosive nitroglycerin with an absorbent mineral called diatomaceous earth, making it far safer to transport and handle. The fortune he earned from dynamite and other explosives patents later funded the Nobel Prizes, established in his 1895 will.

components.note: 宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
自 (nose) — the breath passing through.
心 (heart) — the breath of life, giving 息 its meaning 'to breathe; to rest; news.'

example.hanzi: 愿逝者在天堂安息。
example.pinyin: Yuàn shìzhě zài tiāntáng ānxī.
example.english: May the departed rest in peace in heaven.
example.fact: The ancient Parthian Empire, which controlled much of Persia and Mesopotamia from around 247 BC to 224 AD, was famous for a cavalry tactic later named the “Parthian shot,” in which mounted archers would feign retreat and then twist backward in the saddle to fire arrows at pursuing enemies. Roman armies suffered several major defeats, including at the Battle of Carrhae in 53 BC, before adapting to counter it.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 召 describes calling out to summon someone.
刀 (dāo) gives a rhyme close to zhào, with a different initial.
Mouth — calling out is done with the mouth.
Gives the sound huàn, matching the character's reading.

example.hanzi: 号角声召唤士兵们回到营地。
example.pinyin: Hàojiǎo shēng zhàohuàn shìbīngmen huídào yíngdì.
example.english: The horn call summoned the soldiers back to camp.
example.fact: During World War I, both sides relied heavily on carrier pigeons to summon reinforcements or relay urgent messages when telephone lines were cut by shellfire. One pigeon, a hen named Cher Ami, was credited with delivering a message that helped save nearly 200 trapped American soldiers in 1918 despite being shot through the chest and leg during the flight.

components.note: 巴 is an ancient pictograph traditionally explained as a coiled snake or a large open jaw; the original picture is debated among scholars. The character was later borrowed purely for its sound, most visibly in 巴士 ('bus'), a transliteration of the English word.

士 is an ancient pictograph usually explained as a battle-axe or ceremonial blade, a status symbol carried by noblemen and warriors — the source of 士's meanings 'gentleman, scholar, soldier.' In modern loanwords like 巴士 ('bus'), it is used purely for its sound.

example.hanzi: 我们坐巴士去了机场。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò bāshì qùle jīchǎng.
example.english: We took the bus to the airport.
example.fact: London introduced the world's first regular horse-drawn omnibus service in 1829, and by 1847 competing operators had begun stacking extra seating on the roof, creating the earliest double-decker buses. That basic two-level layout, later motorized, is still the design behind London's iconic red buses today.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 抵 describes pushing back or propping something up with the hand.
氐 (dī) gives a sound close to dǐ, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.
扌 (hand) — fighting back with bare hands
亢 — the throat, a vulnerable point defended while resisting

example.hanzi: 居民组织起来抵抗洪水。
example.pinyin: Jūmín zǔzhī qǐlái dǐkàng hóngshuǐ.
example.english: The residents organized themselves to resist the flood.
example.fact: Antibiotic resistance in bacteria arises through ordinary natural selection: when an antibiotic kills off most of a bacterial population, any cells carrying a random mutation that helps them survive the drug multiply freely and quickly dominate. The World Health Organization has identified this evolutionary process, accelerated by overuse of antibiotics in medicine and agriculture, as one of the top global public health threats.

components.note: 戈 (a dagger-axe, a weapon) — 战 relates to fighting and war.
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 战 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match.

术 was originally a pictograph of a panicled grain plant, a type of millet. It was borrowed for its sound to build 術 ('technique, art'), formed by placing it inside 行 (road, to travel); the modern simplification kept only this core to stand for the whole meaning, as in 战术, 'tactics.'

example.hanzi: 教练在赛前调整了战术。
example.pinyin: Jiàoliàn zài sài qián tiáozhěngle zhànshù.
example.english: The coach adjusted the tactics before the match.
example.fact: The ancient Greek phalanx, a tight rectangular formation of soldiers holding overlapping shields and long spears, dominated Mediterranean warfare for centuries because it presented an almost unbroken wall of protection against any frontal attack. Its major weakness, exposed flanks and rear, was famously exploited by Theban and later Macedonian commanders who developed more flexible formations to outmaneuver it.

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
关 — a person's arms shown in a waving or embracing gesture, bidding farewell
辶 (to walk) — the person walking away who is being seen off

example.hanzi: 这个软件可以快速传送文件。
example.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ kuàisù chuánsòng wénjiàn.
example.english: This software can transmit files quickly.
example.fact: On May 24, 1844, Samuel Morse sent the first long-distance telegraph message, “What hath God wrought,” from Washington, D.C. to Baltimore over a wire strung along a railway line. The demonstration proved that information could travel far faster than any horse or train, and telegraph networks expanded across the world within a few decades.

components.note: A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
才 depicts a young sprout just breaking through the soil — new growth came to represent budding talent or ability.

example.hanzi: 这家公司一直在寻找优秀人才。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī yìzhí zài xúnzhǎo yōuxiù réncái.
example.english: This company has always been looking for outstanding talent.
example.fact: Renaissance Florence, a city of perhaps 60,000 people, produced an extraordinary concentration of artistic talent, including Leonardo da Vinci, Michelangelo, and Botticelli, largely because wealthy families like the Medici competed to sponsor workshops, commissions, and apprenticeships. That patronage system gave promising young artists steady income and training that would have been unavailable in most other cities of the time.

components.note: 千 (thousand) — 重 pictures a heavy burden carried a great distance.
里 (a unit of distance, like a mile) — carrying something a thousand 里 emphasizes how heavy and significant a burden it is, giving 重 its meaning 'heavy' or 'important.'
廴 (to move forward, extend) — 建 relates to constructing or setting something up over an extended process.
聿 (yù) gives a hint of the sound — 建 is pronounced jiàn, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 战后，这座城市花了十年重建。
example.pinyin: Zhàn hòu, zhè zuò chéngshì huāle shí nián chóngjiàn.
example.english: After the war, this city spent ten years rebuilding.
example.fact: After World War II left Warsaw's Old Town almost completely destroyed, Polish architects rebuilt it brick by brick between 1949 and 1963 using pre-war photographs, measured drawings, and even 18th-century paintings by the Venetian artist Bernardo Bellotto as reference. UNESCO later added the reconstructed district to its World Heritage List specifically because of the scale and precision of that restoration effort.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 批 relates to an action done by hand, such as marking or sorting
比 (bǐ) gives a loose sound connection to 批's reading pī
讠 (speech) — 评 relates to speaking judgments or opinions about something
平 (píng) gives the sound — an exact match with 评's reading píng

example.hanzi: 老师严厉地批评了他的作业。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī yánlì de pīpíngle tā de zuòyè.
example.english: The teacher harshly criticized his homework.
example.fact: The Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society, first published in 1665, is credited with introducing formal peer review to scientific publishing, requiring that submitted papers be checked and criticized by other experts before appearing in print. That practice of routine expert criticism became the backbone of how scientific claims are still vetted today.

components.note: 讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō
Traditionally analyzed as 日 combined with 疋, linked to the idea of speaking directly and truthfully — the source of 是's meaning 'to be, indeed, right.'

example.hanzi: 大家都说是他先动手的。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu shuōshì tā xiān dòngshǒu de.
example.english: Everyone says that he was the one who struck first.
example.fact: In the childhood game known as “telephone” or “Chinese whispers,” a short message whispered from person to person along a chain reliably comes out garbled by the end, even in groups of only a dozen people. Psychologists studying rumor transmission have used the same setup to show how each retelling tends to sharpen a few dramatic details while dropping nuance, a pattern also seen in how rumors spread through real communities.

components.note: 氵 (water) — the water that is deep.
罙 (deep) — combined with water, giving 深 its meaning 'deep.'
入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.

example.hanzi: 科学家们深入研究了这种病毒。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen shēnrù yánjiūle zhè zhǒng bìngdú.
example.english: The scientists studied this virus in depth.
example.fact: The Challenger Deep, located in the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific, plunges to about 10,935 meters below sea level, making it the deepest known point in any of Earth's oceans. Only a handful of crewed vehicles, starting with the Trieste in 1960 and including James Cameron's 2012 solo dive, have ever reached its floor.

components.note: 尺 (a ruler/measure) — represents rules or measures being set.
口 (mouth) — measures being discussed aloud in one place gave 局 its meaning 'bureau, office, situation.'
面 was originally a pictograph of a human face, with an outline around an eye — later broadening to mean 'face, surface, side.'

example.hanzi: 谈判陷入了僵持的局面。
example.pinyin: Tánpàn xiànrùle jiāngchí de júmiàn.
example.english: The negotiation fell into a deadlocked situation.
example.fact: During the Cuban Missile Crisis in October 1962, the United States and the Soviet Union came within what historians widely regard as the closest the Cold War ever came to nuclear war, after American reconnaissance flights discovered Soviet missile sites being built in Cuba. The standoff was resolved within thirteen days through secret negotiations in which the U.S. quietly agreed not to invade Cuba in exchange for the missiles' removal.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 操 relates to controlling or handling something.
喿 (zào) gives a sound distantly related to cāo, having drifted apart over time.
纟 (thread) — 纵 originally described letting a thread run loose, extended to mean 'to indulge, release.'
从 (cóng) gives a sound close to zòng.

example.hanzi: 飞行员通过操纵杆操纵飞机。
example.pinyin: Fēixíngyuán tōngguò cāozònggǎn cāozòng fēijī.
example.english: The pilot operates the aircraft using the control stick.
example.fact: Modern airliners increasingly use fly-by-wire systems, in which a pilot's movements of the control stick are converted into electronic signals that a computer interprets before adjusting the control surfaces, rather than moving them through direct mechanical linkages. Airbus introduced the first commercial fly-by-wire jet, the A320, in 1988, and the approach is now standard across most large modern aircraft.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 逃 means to escape or flee, involving movement.
兆 (zhào) gives a rhyme close to táo, with the initial shifted.
亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'

example.hanzi: 他们连夜逃离了着火的房子。
example.pinyin: Tāmen liányè táolíle zháohuǒ de fángzi.
example.english: They fled the burning house in the middle of the night.
example.fact: In June 1962, three inmates, Frank Morris and brothers John and Clarence Anglin, escaped from the supposedly inescapable Alcatraz federal prison by chiseling through the walls of their cells with sharpened spoons and paddling away on a raft made from raincoats. Despite an extensive FBI manhunt, none of the three were ever conclusively found, and the case remains officially unsolved.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 设's meaning 'to establish, set up,' something first proposed through words.
殳 (shū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shè.
罒 (a net) — 置 originally meant to set a net in place
直 (zhí) gives a sound close to 置's reading zhì, sharing a similar historical pronunciation

example.hanzi: 请在手机里设置一个新密码。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài shǒujī lǐ shèzhì yí gè xīn mìmǎ.
example.english: Please set up a new password on your phone.
example.fact: The world's first electric traffic signal was installed at a junction in London in 1868, designed by railway engineer J. P. Knight and operated manually by a police constable who raised colored semaphore arms and lit gas lamps at night. It exploded within weeks after a gas leak injured the officer operating it, and traffic signals did not reappear widely until automated electric versions spread through American cities in the 1910s.

components.note: 回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'
The base of 应 preserves a trace of 心 (heart, mind), reflecting the traditional 應's link to an inner, felt reaction — the root of meanings like 'to respond' and 'to answer.'
应 simplifies 應, whose original phonetic element was a bird-related term read yīng; that ancient reading survives in one of 应's two modern pronunciations, yīng, as in 应该 (yīnggāi, 'should').

example.hanzi: 公司还没有对这条消息做出回应。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī hái méiyǒu duì zhè tiáo xiāoxi zuòchū huíyìng.
example.english: The company has not yet responded to this piece of news.
example.fact: Bats navigate and hunt in complete darkness using echolocation, emitting rapid ultrasonic clicks and interpreting the timing and pitch of the echoes that bounce back off nearby objects and insects. Some species can detect prey as thin as a human hair and adjust their calls in real time depending on how cluttered or open their surroundings are.

components.note: 氵 (water) shows this relates to liquid, as in something boiling or rolling in water.
衮 (gǔn) gives the exact sound of 滚.
虫 (a small creature) — 蛋 names an egg, historically grouped together with small creatures like insects and reptiles.
延 (yán) is only distantly related in sound to dàn — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.

example.hanzi: 他生气地喊道：“你给我滚蛋！”
example.pinyin: Tā shēngqì de hǎndào: “Nǐ gěi wǒ gǔndàn!”
example.english: He shouted angrily, “Get out of here!”
example.fact: Tumbleweeds, most commonly the plant Salsola tragus in North America, are not native to the continent at all; they arrived accidentally from Eurasia with contaminated grain shipments in the 1870s. Once the plant dries out and its stem snaps at the base, wind sends the whole rounded skeleton rolling across open ground, scattering thousands of seeds along the way.

components.note: 丿 (something falling) — an object slipping away.
夫 (a hand/person) — the object slipping out of a hand, giving 失 its meaning 'to lose.'

业 simplifies 業, a pictograph of a notched wooden rack used to hang bells and chime-stones or to post public notices. The association with a fixed workstation or assigned task gave rise to 业's meanings 'occupation, trade, undertaking.'

example.hanzi: 疫情期间，很多人都失业了。
example.pinyin: Yìqíng qījiān, hěnduō rén dōu shīyè le.
example.english: During the pandemic, many people lost their jobs.
example.fact: At the depth of the Great Depression in 1933, the unemployment rate in the United States reached roughly 25 percent, meaning one in four workers had no job. It took nearly a decade of New Deal programs and, ultimately, the industrial mobilization for World War II before employment returned to pre-Depression levels.

components.note: 禾 (a grain plant) — a sweet-smelling crop
日 — here standing in for sweetness (originally 甘), giving the sense of a pleasant smell
火 (fire) — smoke, 烟's meaning, rises from fire.
因 (yīn) gives a rhyme close to yān, with the tone shifted.

example.hanzi: 医生建议他尽快戒掉香烟。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì tā jǐnkuài jièdiào xiāngyān.
example.english: The doctor advised him to quit cigarettes as soon as possible.
example.fact: The 1964 report of the U.S. Surgeon General was the first major government document to formally conclude that cigarette smoking causes lung cancer, drawing on over 7,000 studies reviewed by an advisory committee. It led directly to mandatory warning labels on cigarette packages in 1965 and reshaped decades of public health policy worldwide.

components.note: 毛 (hair) — 毫 originally meant a fine, thin hair.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'

example.hanzi: 面对困难，他毫不犹豫地站了出来。
example.pinyin: Miànduì kùnnán, tā háobù yóuyù de zhànle chūlái.
example.english: Facing difficulty, he stepped forward without any hesitation.
example.fact: Gold leaf can be hammered so thin, down to around 100 nanometers, that light actually passes through it with a faint greenish tint, a thickness roughly a thousand times finer than a human hair. Traditional goldbeaters achieve this by repeatedly pounding and folding the metal between layers of specially treated parchment.

components.note: 丬 (a stylized bed) — 将 originally pictured someone preparing for bed at night.
夕 (evening/night) — the coming of night was seen as predictable, giving 将 its meaning 'about to' or 'going to' happen.
女 (woman) with 覀 depicting hands on the waist — an old image of insisting or demanding something, connected to 要's meaning 'to want, to need.'

example.hanzi: 这座桥将要在明年完工。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò qiáo jiāngyào zài míngnián wángōng.
example.english: This bridge is going to be completed next year.
example.fact: Astronomers calculate that in roughly five billion years, the Sun will exhaust the hydrogen fuel in its core and swell into a red giant large enough to engulf Mercury and Venus, and possibly reach as far as Earth's orbit. Long before that, in about a billion years, rising solar luminosity is expected to boil away Earth's oceans entirely.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 问 relates to speaking, specifically asking a question.
门 (mén) gives a hint of the sound — 问 is pronounced wèn, related but the tone and vowel have shifted.
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'

example.hanzi: 见到老师，别忘了问好。
example.pinyin: Jiàndào lǎoshī, bié wàngle wènhǎo.
example.english: When you see the teacher, don't forget to say hello.
example.fact: Each of NASA's two Voyager probes, launched in 1977, carries a golden phonograph record containing spoken greetings in 55 different human languages, along with music, natural sounds, and images of Earth, intended as a message to any intelligent life that might one day encounter the spacecraft. Both Voyagers have since left the heliosphere and are now traveling through interstellar space.

components.note: 又 (a hand) — reaching out to try to catch something.
隹 (a bird) — catching a bird by hand is hard, giving 难 its meaning 'difficult.'
忄 (heart radical) ties 怪 to an inner emotional reaction — the sense of feeling that something is strange or unexpected, as in 难怪, 'no wonder.'
This 圣 is an unrelated phonetic element, distinct from the character meaning 'holy'; its ancient pronunciation was close to guài, anchoring 怪's modern sound.

example.hanzi: 他昨晚没睡好，难怪今天这么累。
example.pinyin: Tā zuówǎn méi shuìhǎo, nánguài jīntiān zhème lèi.
example.english: He didn't sleep well last night, no wonder he's so tired today.
example.fact: In clinical trials, patients given a completely inactive sugar pill, but told it is a real painkiller, often report measurable reductions in pain, a phenomenon known as the placebo effect. Brain imaging studies have found that placebos can trigger the release of the body's own natural painkillers, called endorphins, which helps explain why patients sometimes genuinely feel better with no active drug at all.

components.note: 十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'
卩 (a person) — the one being dressed.
月 (a garment shape) — a hand 又 placing a coat on the person, giving 服 its meaning 'clothes; to obey, submit.'

example.hanzi: 团队最终克服了所有困难。
example.pinyin: Tuánduì zuìzhōng kèfúle suǒyǒu kùnnán.
example.english: The team ultimately overcame all the difficulties.
example.fact: When an oxygen tank exploded aboard Apollo 13 in April 1970, the three astronauts and mission control in Houston had to improvise a series of workarounds, including building a makeshift carbon dioxide filter out of a plastic bag, cardboard, and duct tape, to survive the four-day trip back to Earth. All three astronauts returned safely, and the mission is often cited as one of NASA's greatest examples of problem-solving under pressure.
